description: This plot, titled “Search Space of M-Cube,” illustrates the number of possible solutions as a function of the number of missing pieces for two different configurations of the M-Cube puzzle. The x-axis, labeled “# Missing pieces,” uses a linear scale ranging from 1 to 6, with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled “# Possible solutions,” uses a logarithmic scale spanning from 10² to 10⁸, with tick marks at intervals of 10⁴. The plot contains two lines: a gold line with circular markers representing the “CUBE-easy” configuration, and a light blue line with circular markers representing the “Flip ignored” configuration. The gold line starts at approximately 10² solutions when 1 piece is missing and increases to 10⁸ solutions when 6 pieces are missing, passing through approximately 10³ solutions at 2 missing pieces and 10⁵ solutions at 4 missing pieces. The light blue line starts at approximately 10² solutions when 1 piece is missing and increases to approximately 10⁶ solutions when 6 pieces are missing, passing through approximately 10³ solutions at 2 missing pieces and 10⁴ solutions at 3 missing pieces. Both lines show a steady increase in the number of possible solutions as the number of missing pieces increases.
